rv.q: Stranger Things’ Noah Schnapp stars in this baffling head-on collision of two plays
Unfortunately there’s not an ounce of subtlety in the script or Sandberg’s direction.

Everyone tries their best to lift the material which despite a rock solid premise and strong opening, meanders into surreal territory with clunkily-written linking scenes and the over-egged Reality TV segment.
Affluenza begins with a provocative premise and an intriguing moral question, but ultimately loses confidence in the very story it sets out to tell.
In fact, I can genuinely say it goes on one of the most head-scratchingly befuddling narrative trajectories I’ve ever seen on stage.

The most interesting thing about the new play Schnapp from Netflix’s Stranger Things has chosen for his stage debut is the dramatic rug pull it executes at the beginning of its 2nd act transforming the audience’s perspective.

cn.t: Critics savage Affluenza as incoherent and sophomoric, with some citing a second-act twist that divides opinion. Most find Sandberg's morality tale about wealth and justice fails to deliver on its premise.
